result.title: Large-scale Model Merging via Recovery-aware Task Weighting
result.summary: Model merging combines multiple task-specific expert models into a single model. However, merging preserves expert capabilities unevenly across tasks. This imbalance is particularly pronounced in large-scale settings, where some tasks can suffer severe capability losses even when average accuracy remains high. To address this imbalance, we introduce Recovery-aware Task Weighting (RaTW), a model merging framework that assigns larger weights to tasks whose expert capabilities are poorly retained by an initial merged model. We quantify these recovery opportunities as the fraction of a task's labeled validation samples that its expert predicts correctly but the initial merged model gets wrong, and use the resulting task weights to re-merge the experts. To evaluate merging at large scale, we construct CLIPMerge-100, a 100-task benchmark with task-specific experts on CLIP ViT-L/14 and ViT-B/32. Across eleven merging methods with 20, 50, and 100 tasks on two CLIP backbones, RaTW improves both mean accuracy and tail20 (the mean expert-normalized accuracy of the 20% worst-retained tasks) in all 33 ViT-L/14 settings and 32 of 33 ViT-B/32 settings. We further introduce ReForge++, which combines RaTW with iterative model refinement and outperforms all evaluated baselines, including a matched-budget control, in both mean accuracy and tail20 across all settings.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 RaTW，用「专家预测正确而初始合并模型错误」的验证样本比例量化各任务的恢复机会，据此给保留较差的任务更大权重并重新合并专家，同时构建 100 任务 CLIPMerge-100 基准与迭代式 ReForge++。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以样本级保留缺口诊断并重分配任务权重的做法，或可供核查多任务/多专家组合时视觉能力丢失的定位与贡献分配，但原文不涉及 latent 推理状态或推理期计算。
